answer: We define a mechanism where dynamic opportunity-cost bonds function as a cryptographic kernel, anchoring identity to staking collateral that provides a basalt security layer. An adversary attempting Sybil multiplication must deploy an atlas of zero-knowledge verifiable delay proofs, ensuring the marginal cost of slashed assets outweighs the aggregate reward. By applying subgame-perfect slashing matrices, the expected utility of such attacks remains strictly negative, forcing convergence to a stable Nash equilibrium.
